fabs.name: Semiconductor Complex Limited (SCL)
fabs.operator: Ministry of Electronics & IT, Govt. of India
fabs.newsQuery: Semiconductor Complex Limited SCL Mohali India
fabs.brief: India's oldest operational semiconductor fab, run directly by the Ministry of Electronics & IT. Specializes in custom ASICs at 180nm for ISRO's satellite payloads and DRDO's defense systems. Not commercially oriented — its output goes almost entirely into India's strategic space and defense programs.

fabs.name: SPEL Semiconductor
fabs.brief: One of India's oldest private-sector semiconductor facilities, focused on outsourced assembly, testing, and packaging (OSAT) rather than wafer fabrication. Takes bare dies manufactured elsewhere and packages them into final chip form — a critical step in the semiconductor supply chain. Serves automotive and consumer electronics customers.

fabs.name: Micron Semiconductor ATP Facility
fabs.techNode: Assembly, Test & Packaging — DRAM & NAND Flash
fabs.newsQuery: Micron Technology semiconductor India Sanand Gujarat
fabs.brief: Micron's first semiconductor facility in India, inaugurated in February 2026 — making it one of the first foreign-owned semiconductor plants to go live under India's semiconductor mission. Assembles, tests, and packages DRAM and NAND flash memory chips for smartphones, laptops, servers, and automotive systems. Micron is the world's third-largest memory chip maker.

fabs.name: Tata Electronics / PSMC Fab
fabs.newsQuery: Tata Electronics PSMC semiconductor fab Dholera India
fabs.brief: India's most ambitious true semiconductor fab — a 300mm AI-enabled wafer fabrication plant targeting 50,000 wafer starts per month at 28nm–110nm nodes. A special economic zone was notified in April 2026. Jointly developed with Taiwan's PSMC. First silicon is targeted for late 2026, with the fab primarily serving automotive, industrial, and consumer electronics markets.

fabs.name: CG Power / Renesas OSAT
fabs.operator: CG Power (India) + Renesas Electronics (Japan) + Stars Microelectronics (Thailand)
fabs.newsQuery: CG Power Renesas semiconductor fab India
fabs.brief: India's first full-service OSAT provider, inaugurated in August 2025. A tri-nation joint venture between India's CG Power, Japan's Renesas, and Thailand's Stars Microelectronics. The G1 facility handles around 0.5 million chip units per day and is scaling toward commercial production capacity. Produces analog and power management chips essential for automotive and industrial systems.

fabs.name: Kaynes Semicon OSAT
fabs.brief: Inaugurated in March 2026 with a production capacity of around 6 million chips per day. Kaynes Technology specializes in high-reliability chip packaging for sectors where failure is not an option — automotive, medical, and aerospace. Advanced packaging technologies like system-in-package (SiP) can combine multiple chips into a single compact, high-performance module.

fabs.name: ISMC Analog Fab
fabs.newsQuery: ISMC semiconductor fab India Karnataka Mysuru
fabs.brief: A proposed analog semiconductor fab originally backed by UAE-based Next Orbit Ventures in consortium with Tower Semiconductor (Israel). The project stalled after the primary investor withdrew and Intel's acquisition of Tower fell through. The Indian government is actively working to revive this project, as a 65nm analog fab would complement the logic fabs being built in Gujarat.

fabs.name: HCL – Foxconn OSAT
fabs.newsQuery: HCL Foxconn semiconductor OSAT India Jewar
fabs.brief: A joint venture between HCL and Foxconn for semiconductor assembly and testing near the upcoming Noida International Airport, approved by the Union Cabinet in May 2025. Notably focused on wafer-level packaging (WLP) of display driver ICs — an advanced packaging technique not previously adopted by any India OSAT project. Foxconn owns a 40% stake. Proximity to a major air cargo hub is deliberate, as chips move by air.

fabs.name: CDIL Semiconductors Expansion
fabs.newsQuery: CDIL Continental Device India semiconductor Mohali expansion
fabs.brief: CDIL is one of India's oldest private semiconductor manufacturers (founded 1964), now expanding its Mohali plant under the India Semiconductor Mission. The expansion targets high-power discrete devices — MOSFETs, IGBTs, and SiC components used in solar inverters, EV powertrains, and industrial motor drives. Annual capacity will grow from 600 million to over 760 million units, with 158 million being high-power discrete chips.

fabs.name: RIR Power Electronics SiC Fab
fabs.newsQuery: RIR Power Electronics silicon carbide semiconductor Odisha Bhubaneswar
fabs.brief: India's first Silicon Carbide (SiC) semiconductor fabrication plant, backed by the Odisha state government. SiC chips are critical for next-generation power electronics — they handle far higher voltages and temperatures than conventional silicon, making them essential for EV inverters, solar converters, and industrial power grids. SiC wafer epitaxy production is targeted from 2026, with phased commercial rollout thereafter.

fabs.name: Crystal Matrix GaN / MicroLED Fab
fabs.newsQuery: Crystal Matrix GaN microLED semiconductor Dholera India
fabs.brief: India's first Gallium Nitride (GaN) based mini/micro-LED display fabrication facility, approved by the Union Cabinet in May 2026. GaN enables displays that are far brighter, more energy-efficient, and longer-lasting than OLED or LCD — the technology behind next-generation TVs, AR/VR headsets, and automotive dashboards. The facility will produce 6-inch GaN wafers and full display modules, targeting 72,000 sq. metres of display panels annually.
